source.title: Learning to Generalize Provably in Learning to Optimize
source.authors: Junjie Yang; Tian-Long Chen; Mingkang Zhu; Fengxiang He; Da-Cheng Tao; Yitao Liang; Zhang-Yang Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether flatness-aware regularization of learned optimizers improves optimizee test performance, using L2O meta-training and unseen optimizees rather than the claim versions’ standard-training recipes.
record.gate_note: Results on learned optimizers and their trained optimizees are this study’s own; cited findings about SGD, Adam, sharp minima, and Entropy-SGD are not counted as rows. Figures 2–5 report several training-loss and test-accuracy comparisons, but the supplied text gives no precise figure values except explicitly stated accuracies and table values.
record.test_reason: Supplementary Section A.4 directly compares SGD and Adam test accuracy on Conv-MNIST across the same five learning rates, bearing on V4 under limited tuning. The main learned-optimizer experiments do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Hessian and local-entropy regularizers can meta-train learned optimizers to favor flat landscapes and improve optimizee test performance. They also establish conditional theoretical bounds and report practical differences between regularizers across optimizees.
record.recipe_differences: The study meta-trains learned optimizers with Hessian or local-entropy regularizers, then evaluates optimizee training and test accuracy. It does not test the original claim’s standard-training setups for memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness-gap correlation, or memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularizer type and approximation, L2O algorithm, optimizee architecture and dataset change reported outcomes; Entropy is reported as better on Conv-MNIST and Conv-CIFAR, while Hessian is better on MLP-ReLU and Conv-Large-MNIST; Hessian Trace is described as the most stable and substantial approximation variant.

fits_no_version.finding: Flatness-aware meta-training improves learned-optimizer performance in the reported comparisons, with benefits depending on regularizer and optimizee. Direct Hessian regularization of SGD improves Conv-MNIST accuracy but reduces Conv-CIFAR accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian- or entropy-based regularization can improve optimizee test accuracy, with outcomes depending on the optimizer, architecture, and dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2023
record.problems: Several central comparisons are presented only in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The reported tables provide no uncertainty estimates. The text reports that the vanilla L2O-DM-CL fails to train Conv-Large-MNIST and that even its Hessian-regularized variant has unsatisfactory training loss, despite improved test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: The main text describes figure comparisons for MLP-ReLU, Conv-MNIST, Conv-Large-MNIST and Conv-CIFAR in Figures 2–4, and ResNet-20 in Figure 5, without recoverable numeric values in the text; no separate rows were retained for those figure-only comparisons beyond the explicitly described Conv-Large-MNIST and ResNet-20 findings.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, broader tuning, decay-schedule effects, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and whether Adam achieves equal or better training performance in the Section A.4 comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, correlation with training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Add the SGD–Adam learning-rate comparison: rates 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, 0.00001 yield SGD accuracies 9.81%, 78.01%, 80.84%, 11.09%, 10.82%, and Adam accuracies 9.80%, 9.95%, 72.44%, 55.89%, 64.84%. Best-of-grid SGD exceeds Adam by 8.40 percentage points. Table 5's learning-rate header incorrectly says SGD, but its caption and surrounding text identify Adam.

record.verdict_notes: The main experiments use unscaled Hessian and local-entropy regularizers, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Theoretical excess-population-risk bounds also do not establish V7's empirical gap-ranking claim. Figure-only comparisons already declared in rows_left_out are not additional missing results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under varying tuning breadth.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with training set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.
